$comment: The package ledger. Every source file in this repo belongs to exactly one
package, and scripts/check-packages.mjs fails if that stops being true.
This file exists because of a diagnosis, not a preference: reepub started
(2026-05-28) with the right division — Swift for what only Swift can do
(Vision OCR), Node for assembly. It drifted twice. On 2026-06-14 the app
needed to be offline and self-sufficient, so assembly was rebuilt in Swift;
that is where 'one implementation' broke. Between 2026-07-30 and 08-01 five
more modules appeared, all Node-only, in three days.
Nobody chose that. Sessions without memory of how the repo grew kept
building in whichever direction was convenient, and Node is the convenient
one. A ledger a machine reads is the only kind that survives that, which is
why 'sources' is enforced rather than documented.
Decision 2026-08-02 (see HANDOFF.md): the assembly core moves to Swift,
because Vision OCR cannot leave it and offline quality is what the product
stands on. 'target' records where each file is headed; 'sources' records
where it actually is today. They are allowed to disagree — that gap IS the
migration. What is not allowed is a file belonging to neither.

scan-ocr.purpose: PDF → one JSON line per recognised text line, with bounding boxes. Apple Vision. No EPUB knowledge whatsoever.

epub-kit.purpose: The assembly core: package document, navigation document, NCX, chapter XHTML, cover HTML. The one implementation, per decision A.

epub-text.purpose: XML and text plumbing: escaping, serialisation, entity decoding, pictograph stripping. Seven modules import it and every one of them is alive.

epub-binder.purpose: Emits package documents from Node for heal / merge / web-ingest. Transitional by construction: it is the second assembler, and the boundary gate lists it as a known one until those callers drive epub-kit instead.
epub-binder.target: epub-kit — Node tools should call the Swift binary rather than emit their own <package>

epub-doctor.purpose: Operates on finished EPUBs: validate, heal, merge. Never touches OCR, never rasterises a cover — which is what keeps its dependency budget to one library.

epub-cover.purpose: Typesets a cover and rasterises it through a browser. Separated from epub-doctor so that package can be installed without downloading Chromium — a lazy require would not have helped, because the dependency is charged at install time, not at load time.
epub-cover.target: the typesetting half moves to epub-kit (Swift) and emits HTML; this package keeps only the Node rasteriser, with WKWebView as the app's

web-ingest.purpose: A web page reduced to structure: strip layout, translate classes, dehydrate images. The base a web→md exporter would sit on.

ocr-builder-node.purpose: The Node path from OCR output to EPUB, and the paragraph heuristics only it uses. This is the ONLY code genuinely duplicated by EpubBuilder.swift.
ocr-builder-node.freezeCondition: flips to "frozen" when the CLI builds through epub-kit. Kept, not strangled — but kept as a FILE, never as a documented way to use reepub.

app.purpose: The product. SwiftUI, offline, consumes scan-ocr + epub-kit.

cli.purpose: Thin surfaces over the cores: local web UI, the web→EPUB entry point, the image optimizer.

_tests.purpose: Suites. Not a shipped package; claimed here so no test file counts as unowned.

_tooling.purpose: Repo-level guards and fetchers. Not shipped.
